findings.summary: The check command itself is neither typechecked nor executed by any recorded gate: tsconfig.json's include is ["src","test"], so scripts/verify-protocol.ts is outside `npm run typecheck`, and the implement handoff's verification record ran only npm ci / typecheck / test / smoke:cas -- never `npm run verify:protocol`. The dual-source diff is still proven green, because test/protocol-contract.test.ts calls the same verifyConsumerContract against the real committed snapshot and generated artifact, but a regression confined to the CLI wrapper would go unnoticed.

verifyConsumerContract and renderGeneratedProtocol hard-code the three research.* kinds via literal snapshot.protocols["research.clue.v2"] lookups and per-kind blocks, so the spec's "any consumer (deep-research, chatgroup, future domains)" can reuse the kind-generic primitives (canonicalJson/computeDigest/verifyRegistryRecord/derive*/resolveProtocol) but must reimplement the top-level diff and renderer for its own kinds.

The transition-graph source comparison is guarded by `if (committed)`, so a snapshot with clue_state_machine removed would leave only the weaker "transition values are within the registry status enum" check and `npm run verify:protocol` could exit 0. The hole is closed in practice by npm test, since renderGeneratedProtocol throws on a missing clue_state_machine and the "generated artifact === rendered" test then fails.

Carried forward from the Continuous review and re-confirmed: PENDING_CLUE_STATUSES is a hand-written partition of the clue status enum into pending vs terminal groups, not derived from protocol.generated. It is outside the spec's scope (field names, kinds, transitions in src/protocol.ts), but a registry-added status would not auto-update it.
